ledger.x: 1856: the State of Venezuela becomes the Republic.
1864: the United States of Venezuela, after the Federal War (1859-63).
1877: Cliopatria's outline shrinks by seven cells on the British Guiana side (about 1,800 km2).
1877: four cells are added on the Brazilian side.
1899: the Paris Award gives Venezuela the Orinoco mouth.
1999: the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, 'the full official title since the adoption of the Constitution of 1999' (20 December 1999).

wars.name: Federal War
wars.outcome: A civil war without territorial change; 'This culminated in the Federal War (1859-63)' and the state became the United States of Venezuela in 1864.

wars.name: Venezuela crisis of 1895
wars.outcome: The Paris Arbitral Award of 3 October 1899 gave Britain most of the disputed territory and all of the gold mines, and Venezuela Barima Point and the river's mouth; demarcation 1900-1905.

wars.name: Venezuela crisis of 1902-1903
wars.outcome: Britain, Germany and Italy 'imposed a naval blockade'; no change of border.

wars.name: Guayana Esequiba dispute
wars.outcome: Unsettled: Venezuela denounced the 1899 award before the United Nations in 1945 and 'formally raised the issue again' there in 1962, the Geneva Agreement was signed on 17 February 1966, Venezuelan troops occupied Ankoko Island in October 1966, the ICJ…

certainty.note: The British Guiana frontier was disputed (Schomburgk Line 1840-1886, award 1899); the Brazilian line was a treaty from 5 May 1859 but undemarcated, and the Colombian line rested on the 1891 award; the pages give no surveys.
The British Guiana frontier follows the 1899 award demarcated 1900-1905, the Brazilian line the 1859 treaty ratified by the 1929 protocol, the Colombian line the 1891 award and the 1941 treaty.
